_README: Deployment presets for liveClassifierTorchROS.py. This file is COMMITTED TO GIT so a
deployment site picks up new models and operating points with a plain `git pull` --
no environment variables to set on-site.
The FIRST entry of "configurations" is the one used at startup. To switch, either
reorder the list (and commit) or pass the preset name as an argument:
ros2 run magician_vision_classifier liveClassifierTorchROS --config low_false_alarm
The model's .pth/.json are auto-downloaded on first run from
http://ammar.gr/magician/models/CameraV2Models/ (ModelDownload.ensure_model), the same
directory scripts/uploadModels.sh pushes to.
gate.threshold semantics depend on gate.mode. Under the default "defect_mass" it
thresholds 1 - P(clean) -- the total probability mass on ANY defect class -- NOT the
max softmax probability. A max_prob threshold of the same number means something
completely different. Thresholds are NOT portable between models: re-read them from
that model's <name>_threshold_curve.json.
Every number under "measured" is read from the named threshold-curve file, not
estimated. They come from the run's held-out split, which was ALSO used to select the
checkpoint, so treat the absolute values as slightly optimistic -- the ranking between
operating points is sound (see ISSUES.md M3).
2026-08-26 UPDATE -- READ BEFORE TRUSTING THE NUMBERS BELOW.
Model switched from fzcnxtiny_convnext_tiny (Aug26_78K, recording-disjoint coverage
carve-out, see the 2026-08-25 note preserved below) to ttcnxpico_convnext_pico -- a
FRESH convnext_pico retrain from `EXPERIMENT-traintest-split-sweep.md`'s in-distribution
train/test campaign. This switch was made WITHOUT the standard generalization safeguard
the rest of this file's history relies on:
- There is NO TIER_A / recording-disjoint coverage number for this checkpoint.
`eval_coverage.py` was never run against it -- this campaign has no coverage
carve-out at all (dataloader.exclude_frames + validation_dataset were both removed
from its config in favour of a RANDOM TILE-LEVEL split, sibling-leakage expected by
design -- see EXPERIMENT-traintest-split-sweep.md §1/§3). We do not know whether
this checkpoint generalises better or worse than fzcnxtiny_convnext_tiny.
- The gate/threshold_reference curve below is ALSO calibrated on that same leaky
random split, not the Aug26_78K factory val -- score_checkpoints.py drives off
whatever build_val_only(cfg) returns for a config, and for this one that is the
frozen_tile_split, not validation_dataset. So even the raw detected/false_alarm
numbers immediately below are optimistic relative to a real held-out set, on top of
the usual same-checkpoint-selection optimism the paragraph above already flags.
- What IS different and real: this run's training set is LARGER than every other run
in the campaign -- it includes the ~3,054 frames every other config carves out for
coverage evaluation (§2.5 of knowledge/24-8-report.md). More data, unknown net effect.
This was an explicit, informed decision (not an oversight) to ship on that basis anyway.
If you are reading this cold: the honest move is to run eval_coverage.py against
ttcnxpico_convnext_pico on the real coverage carve-out before trusting this over the
previous default, then update this note.
runtime.step reverted to 16 -- convnext_pico's own native front-row throughput (36.0 Hz
at step 16, knowledge/24-8-report.md §4/§7) rather than convnext_tiny's coarser step 18,
since the deployed architecture changed back to convnext_pico.

PUBLISHING NOTE, verified 2026-08-26: ttcnxpico_convnext_pico_20260826_025215.zip IS
live at http://ammar.gr/magician/models/CameraV2Models/ (uploadModels.sh runs with
ALLOW_ALL=1 hardcoded, so scripts/upload_allowlist.txt does not actually gate what
reaches the server). Ran the exact startup path end to end against a clean directory
standing in for a deployment box: ensure_model() fetched and extracted the archive,
ClassifierPnm loaded it with zero missing/unexpected state-dict keys, forward pass
produced the expected (1,10) output, and applying this file's 'default' preset produced
the same 90.3% detected / 0.80% false-alarm gate the threshold_reference below states
(on the leaky split -- see the caveat above). Auto-download and use are both confirmed
mechanically working; generalisation is NOT confirmed.

_comment: Measured operating curve for the default model. Read verbatim from
detected = fraction of DEFECT tiles flagged. false_alarm = fraction of CLEAN tiles
flagged; multiply by the tiles-per-frame count to get crosses per frame.
⚠ UNLIKE every earlier version of this file, this curve is measured on the SAME
random, leaky, tile-level split the model trained against (frozen_tile_split, sibling
leakage expected by design) -- NOT the Aug26_78K factory val. Treat every number here
as optimistic relative to a real held-out set, not just 'slightly' as the file-level
README's usual caveat says. See the 2026-08-26 UPDATE note above.
A false-alarm rate below ~0.1% is NOT reachable: the sweep bottoms out at threshold

configurations.name: default
configurations.description: ttcnxpico_convnext_pico -- convnext_pico retrained with the coverage carve-out folded back into training. UNVERIFIED generalisation (no TIER_A coverage run yet) and this curve is measured on the same leaky split it trained on -- read the file-level README's 2026-08-26 UPDATE before trusting these numbers over the previous default.

configurations.name: low_false_alarm
configurations.description: Same model near a 0.5% false-alarm budget on its own (leaky) curve.

configurations.name: minimal_false_alarm
configurations.description: Strictest useful gate on the leaky curve: ~0.21% false alarms. Below roughly 0.1% FA is not reachable on this model.

configurations.name: one_percent_fa
configurations.description: Highest detection available inside a 1% false-alarm budget on the leaky curve.

configurations.name: high_recall
configurations.description: ttcnxpico_convnext_pico at its trainer-calibrated KPI-optimal gate on the leaky curve. Use only where an operator reviews the crosses.
